decision_question: Does the project (a) withdraw the protocol-faithful baseline claim and proceed on other evidence, (b) fund a prospective protocol-faithful baseline study to earn the claim back, or (c) redirect the next unit of compute at the project's central claim, whose control experiment has never been run?

options.name: Declare EXT-03 exploratory and proceed on other evidence
options.action: Accept v1.0/v1.1 disposition as final; report EXT-03 only as a reduced-protocol exploratory ranking and negative-results record; withdraw AS-08 as UNRESOLVED; run no further training.
options.authorization_required: none - this is the default state if no decision is made

options.name: Prospective protocol-faithful baseline study (EXT-04)
options.action: Five architectures x three seeds under the frozen phase09/10 recipe (AdamW, lr 1e-4, wd 1e-4, bce_dice 0.5/0.5 eps 1e-6, full augmentation, 1-channel input, cosine T_max 100, batch 4, patience 15) behind a rebuilt prelaunch gate containing at least one direct edge to the frozen authority comparing concrete values, and binding the executing harness by digest per run.
options.time_to_result: 3-5 weeks including gate construction, gate testing and the negative-control battery
options.risk_detail: Three host terminations during EXT-03 (2026-10-22 ep52, 2026-10-25 ep98, 2026-10-25 segformer ep5) attributed to a failing CMOS battery / RTC drift (5.19 days behind, Time-Service ID 52, offset 448320 s) with no UPS. Launching fifteen more runs before remediation repeats a known, diagnosed, unfixed fault.
options.authorization_required: new work order + frozen protocol-faithful harness + rebuilt gate + battery and UPS remediation + explicit supervisor sign-off (none of which exists)

options.name: FiLM-off control - redirect the next unit of compute at the central claim
options.action: Because the FiLM output projection is zero-initialised, freezing film_layers and task_embedding at initialisation yields a plain residual UNet exactly identical to GlobalMedFiLM at step 0, differing only by the absence of task conditioning during training. Same architecture, same parameter count, same protocol, same seed, same data.
repairs: FiLM attribution (the only option that can)
options.compute: ~10-11 h per seed under the Phase-21 protocol; 22-33 h for three seeds
options.limitation: One seed is a point estimate, not a variance estimate; a defensible claim wants three seeds or an explicit single-seed limitation statement.
options.authorization_required: separate work order + frozen control harness + prelaunch gate + explicit sign-off (not authorised here, not executed here)

comparison_matrix.note: Only one training process may run at a time, so A/B/C are exclusive as next actions.

recommendation.sequencing: C first; B deferred; A as the default if no authorisation is granted.
reasons: The larger gap is the central claim: FiLM attribution is NOT_ESTABLISHED, meaning the project's contribution has no control arm in its own ablation family. A protocol-faithful baseline table strengthens a supporting comparison, not the contribution. Value per unit compute favours C by roughly two orders of magnitude.

C is an order of magnitude cheaper (11 h vs 3 weeks) and more decisive: a positive FiLM-off result is interpretable on its own, whereas B's product is a table that still cannot isolate FiLM because the 0.1694 gap bundles task conditioning, protocol, architecture and seed treatment.

B's expected value is conditional on a framing decision the supervisor has not made. If the manuscript reframes around conditioning rather than a baseline leaderboard, AS-08 stops being load-bearing and B becomes optional.
C does not foreclose B; they are sequential, not exclusive. Doing C first sharpens what the baseline comparison is for and makes the case for or against B on evidence rather than on hope.

A is honest, costs nothing, and is what happens by default. A project that discloses a divergent baseline study and reframes around a controlled result stands better than one that runs fifteen more experiments to protect a table.

decide on seeds 2-3 and on B
